issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Auth Unauthorized Response

Summary

Extracted the repeated unauthorized response from AuthMiddleware.CheckAuth into one private helper. Five identical response blocks now call unauthorized(c) while preserving the existing HTTP status and mobile-facing JSON contract.

Changes

  • Added unauthorized(c *fiber.Ctx) error in AuthMiddleware.go.
  • Kept the original fiber.StatusUnauthorized status.
  • Kept the original {statusCode, data.message} response structure.
  • Replaced five matching literals with return unauthorized(c).
  • Added TestUnauthorizedResponseShape in AuthMiddleware_test.go.

Migrated Branches

The helper is used when:

  1. The Authorization header is missing or empty.
  2. JWT verification returns an invalid status.
  3. The default role cannot be read.
  4. The encoded subject is missing or invalid.
  5. The role is unsupported.

Response Compatibility

The focused test sends a request without an Authorization header and asserts:

  • HTTP status is 401.
  • statusCode is 401.
  • data.message is Unauthorized.
  • No extra fields are present.

Functions.ErrorResponse was not used because it adds status, valid, and errors, which would change the established mobile API response.

Scope Audit

  • 5 helper calls.
  • 1 remaining unauthorized response literal, owned by the helper.
  • 1 middleware implementation file changed.
  • 1 focused test file added.
  • No Slim or Worker file changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Middleware/AuthMiddleware/AuthMiddleware.go src/Middleware/AuthMiddleware/AuthMiddleware_test.go
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • Both Go files are formatted.
  • The focused response compatibility test passes.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

AuthMiddleware.CheckAuth contained five identical unauthorized response blocks. Each block returned HTTP 401 with the same mobile-facing JSON contract:

{
  "statusCode": 401,
  "data": {
    "message": "Unauthorized"
  }
}

Repeating this response made the middleware longer and allowed its failure branches to drift independently.

Scope

  • Add one private unauthorized(c) helper in AuthMiddleware.go.
  • Replace only the five response blocks with an identical HTTP status and JSON body.
  • Add a focused test that locks the response status and body shape.
  • Keep the change inside AuthMiddleware.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • HTTP status 401.
  • Top-level statusCode with value 401.
  • data.message with value Unauthorized.
  • The absence of additional response fields.
  • The same unauthorized branches for missing tokens, invalid tokens, missing roles, invalid subjects, and unsupported roles.

Out of Scope

  • Using Functions.ErrorResponse, because it produces a different JSON schema.
  • Changing token verification, role validation, subject decoding, or Fiber locals.
  • Changing any mobile-facing response field.
  • Updating Slim or Worker files.
  • Refactoring successful authentication flows.

Acceptance Criteria

  • One private helper owns the existing unauthorized response literal.
  • All five identical branches call the helper.
  • No duplicate unauthorized response literal remains in CheckAuth.
  • A focused test verifies the exact HTTP status and decoded JSON structure.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-03. No commit was created.

issues.display_title: Issue #530: Centralize Description Unescaping and Wrapping
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Description Unescaping and Wrapping

Summary

Added PostFunctions.UnescapeAndWrapText and replaced 24 identical unescape-and-wrap pairs across 22 Action files. The helper keeps the existing full, short, and long description behavior without changing any response field or type.

Changes

  • Added UnescapeAndWrapText(description string) (string, map[string]string) in PostsFunctions.go.
  • Replaced each matching html.UnescapeString plus PostFunctions.WrapText pair with one helper call.
  • Removed the resulting unused html imports.
  • Added TestUnescapeAndWrapTextPreservesExistingSequence in PostsFunctions_test.go.

Migrated Scope

  • Bookmarks: 1 call site.
  • Collection posts: 1 call site.
  • Comments: 4 call sites.
  • Node posts: 1 call site.
  • V1 posts: 9 call sites.
  • Search: 1 call site.
  • Supports: 6 call sites across 4 files.
  • V2 posts: 1 call site.

Total: 24 call sites across 22 files.

Response Compatibility

The helper preserves the previous operation order:

description = html.UnescapeString(description)
return description, WrapText(description)

WrapText continues to perform its own HTML unescape. The focused test uses &amp; and verifies that the full value remains &, while the short and long values remain &.

All existing response assignments remain unchanged, including description, comment, short, and long fields. No response schema or model was modified.

Scope Audit

  • 24 helper calls across 22 Action files.
  • No matching duplicate pair remains outside Slim and Worker files.
  • No Slim or Worker file changed.
  • Unrelated standalone HTML unescaping was left unchanged.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -l <changed Go files>
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • The focused behavior-preservation test passes.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

Twenty-four call sites across 22 Action files repeated the same two-step description processing:

desc := html.UnescapeString(description)
wrapped := PostFunctions.WrapText(desc)

The duplicated sequence made related post and comment response flows longer and allowed their HTML decoding and wrapping behavior to drift independently.

Scope

  • Add one shared PostFunctions.UnescapeAndWrapText helper.
  • Replace all 24 matching pairs in the related Action flows.
  • Remove html imports that become unused.
  • Add one focused test for the existing unescape sequence.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • The full description or comment value after one HTML unescape.
  • The short and long values produced by the existing WrapText behavior.
  • The existing second HTML unescape performed inside WrapText.
  • Every existing empty-value guard, assignment target, response field, and response type.
  • Mobile-facing response schemas.

Out of Scope

  • Changing WrapText truncation or token handling.
  • Refactoring unrelated standalone html.UnescapeString calls.
  • Updating Slim or Worker files.
  • Renaming response fields or changing response models.

Acceptance Criteria

  • One helper owns the shared unescape-and-wrap sequence.
  • All 24 matching call sites use the helper.
  • No matching duplicate pair remains outside Slim and Worker files.
  • A focused test locks the existing double-unescape sequence.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-03. No commit was created.
